round1: FAIL — the host guard compared only URL.host, so an https source could be called over plain http and a bearer token would go out in the clear; plus nine should items

items.finding: Host guard ignored the url scheme: http://<allowed host>/ passed and the Authorization header went out unencrypted.
items.fix: fixed round 1: refuse compares URL.origin, refuses userinfo, refuses a non-special scheme, and allows plain http only on loopback and only when a caller opts in

items.finding: Redirects could be followed if a process installed a redirect interceptor on the global dispatcher.
items.fix: fixed round 1: the adapter owns a private undici Agent, and a 3xx is refused; round 2 gave the test a real Location and asserts the target is never called

items.finding: Steps queued behind a permit still reached a source whose breaker had opened.
items.fix: fixed round 1: the breaker is read again under the permit, with a non-consuming state read so the half-open trial survives

items.finding: A failed half-open trial did not re-open the breaker, so a down source was probed on every call.
items.fix: fixed round 1, with a test asserting one probe per cooldown

items.finding: Error verdicts embedded driver messages, which can carry a url and its query string, and reached the log.
items.fix: fixed round 1: a fixed vocabulary, with a redaction test that throws an error containing a token

items.finding: health bypassed guard, permit, breaker and timeout.
items.fix: fixed round 1; round 2 added the no-usable-budget refusal

items.finding: Permits and breakers were keyed by a caller-supplied display name and per adapter instance.
items.fix: fixed round 1: keyed by the allow-listed origin in a shared registry, isolatable for tests

items.finding: Rows were counted only when the body was a top-level array, so {data:[...]} was never capped.
items.fix: fixed round 1: the largest array at depth two or less is counted and capped

items.finding: An abandoned generator left the source working.
items.fix: fixed round 1: ExecContext.signal, including the already-aborted case

items.finding: A catalog that listed POST would let the adapter write; the read-only property rested on catalog hygiene.
items.fix: fixed round 2: a writing method is refused unless the source is marked sandbox (architecture §8), whatever the catalog lists

items.finding: A caller-supplied Host header would route the call and its credential to another site behind the same address.
items.fix: fixed round 2: host and :authority are stripped, with a test

items.finding: A cancelled run and a misconfigured redirect both counted against the breaker and could mark a healthy source down.
items.fix: fixed round 2: neither counts, with tests

items.finding: The loopback http allowance was compiled into the production guard.
items.fix: fixed round 2: it is an explicit option a worker never sets, and the fixtures ask for it

items.finding: probeReadOnly reads the catalog and never probes; ResolvedServer/ResolvedStep are not yet unions on kind.
items.fix: answered: the reason string ends with (not probed), and the union arrives with U-013 rather than being guessed at now

summary: The round-1 block is genuinely closed: refuse compares URL.origin, rejects userinfo, and enforces https except on an opt-in loopback, with a table test covering downgrade, port, scheme, userinfo, case and trailing dot. Nothing opens a write path or leaks a value.
